thread:
anya: heads-up — noticed weird step artifact on the token-level SLO dashboard for p95/p99 in us-west-2 around 03:00 UTC. looks like aggregation changed, panels show a hard jump not mirrored in tokens/sec.

miguel: can you drop the panel id / promql? curious whether it's a rollup or a dashboard transform.

anya: panel id 702 (ttft_p99_tokens_us_west2). query: 
```
avg(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, region))) by (model)
```
I pulled raw logs and raw request timings don't show the same cliff.

samir: we pushed the prometheus rollup change to compact agents at 02:48 UTC to reduce ingested series. it replaced per-shard histogram buckets with summary-style rollups for older samples. might be exposing bucket boundary mismatches.

yuki: earlier at 02:42 we had brief NIC flaps on west2-b (net team incident). could be packet loss causing partial telemetry. but i agree the shape looks like an aggregation artifact.

miguel: two hypotheses: 1) rollup changed bucket boundaries -> histogram_quantile over aggregated buckets gives wrong quantiles; 2) dashboard uses `avg` after quantile instead of quantile after `sum` leading to smoothing/mis-ordering.

anya: ok. can we try a quick dashboard tweak to compare:
- raw: `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, region))`
- safe: `max_over_time(histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(token_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, model, region))[15m:1m])`
- fallback: `quantile_over_time(0.99, token_latency_seconds[15m])` (if we have seconds summary)

samir: i ran the raw vs safe side-by-side in a test dashboard. raw shows the cliff, safe smooths it out. suggests rollup is the cause.

miguel: for an immediate mitigation i recommend: change alert rule eval to use `max_over_time(...[15m])` for p99 to avoid transient bucket artifacts, and add a note on runbook about rollup mismatch.

anya: agreed. that prevents noisy p99 alerts. but we should also quantify cost impact: if GPU throttles during apparent spikes operators may over-provision.

yuki: good call. observed in the same window autoscaler added 6 shards in west2 around 03:10 due to the p95/p99 alert firing. turnover added ~6k tokens/sec capacity, ~0.6 GPUs/hr extra cost for the window.

anya: that aligns with the billing spike I saw in cost-dashboard. if alerts are noisy we risk sustained overprovisioning.

samir: long term fixes: 1) revert or refine rollup so bucket boundaries are preserved for histograms; 2) change compact agent to emit a `token_latency_seconds_count`/`sum` summary compatible with quantile_over_time; 3) add a deploy-time check that ensures histogram buckets are stable across versions.

miguel: i'll open a prometheus-ops PR to pin buckets and to document the agent change.

anya: action items:
- @miguel open PR + link -> due EOD (owner: miguel)
- @samir revert/refine rollup on canary node -> due ASAP (owner: samir)
- @yuki update alert eval to `max_over_time(...[15m])` and mute noisy alert in west2 for 1h -> done? (owner: yuki)

yuki: muting now for channel alerts, still leaving metric recording alone so we can compare. :mute:

dashbot: [alert-silence] created silence 1h for channel=eng-platform scope=west2, id=slc-20240312-001

anya: once PR is up i'll run a head-to-head dashboard and follow up with a short note in #incidents if this caused the autoscaler ramp.

miguel: PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/prometheus-ops/pull/212 -- description: pin histogram buckets in compact agent + compatibility test.

samir: rolling a canary of the refined rollup to west2-c now (build 20240312-r2). will post results in ~10m.

anya: thanks. if canary looks good we'll patch west2 cluster and restore alert evals.

yuki: canary looks stable, no cliff after 7m observation. marking as success.

miguel: merging PR after CI, will coordinate deploy with samir.

anya: great. after deploy let's revert the alert mute and monitor for false positives for next 24h. also i'll add a small dashboard note about "rollup artifact" so oncall knows the history.

samir: deploying cluster-wide patch in 10m.

anya: status update: patch deployed to west2, dashboards show p95/p99 back to expected shape. autoscaler did not trigger additional shards post-fix.

miguel: follow-up: added a unit test to our agent that runs `histogram_quantile` on canonical inputs to detect bucket drift during builds.

anya: closing loop: created a short incident note and cost calc: noisy p99 caused ~0.5 GPU-hrs extra; approximate $3.4 in margin cost. wrote runbook blurb for alert tuning.

yuki: thanks everyone.

anya: :thumbsup:
